correctness.rationale: The Hermite derivative has fixed secant sign under the unit cap, proving exact one-input variation. Decreasing a single affine-plateau secant by epsilon forces both affected slopes to decrease by at least epsilon for every admissible selector. Their two neighboring Hermite bumps yield 16 epsilon/27 in variation and the middle cell at least epsilon. For minmod, absolute-continuity along data homotopies reduces the variation of a unit secant perturbation to a positive unit-integral middle kernel plus at most two 8/27 bump integrals. Exact rational witnesses attain 43/27. Proof covers arbitrary finite-variation bi-infinite real samples; finite checker tests corroborate but do not substitute for the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The larger admissible slope regions in shape-preserving interpolation give a condition for each curve, not a bound on the variation of the difference of two interpolants. Even if one-input preservation is deducible, this does not bound two-input sensitivity. The unit-cap class theorem is narrower in geometry but stronger and different in perturbation quantifiers.

value.rationale: Rather than another fixed-method coefficient, the result resolves a natural method-design minimax question for every local affine-exact conservative slope rule: the unit-cap condition that ensures shape preservation forces at least 43/27 sensitivity between two inputs, and a simple standard limiter is optimal. This separates one-input TV preservation from perturbation stability and yields a sharp impossibility frontier for noise-sensitive interpolation.
